members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in post_writer: the task group spawns post_writer but the caller could proceed (and start sending/expecting messages) before post_writer's stream context was actually entered and ready, causing lost or hung messages during streamable-http POST writes. Both PRs fix it identically by adding a `task_status: TaskStatus[None]` parameter to `post_writer` and calling `task_status.started(None)` once the write-stream context is entered, so `tg.start()` callers block until post_writer is truly ready.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Race condition in post_writer: the task group spawns post_writer but the caller could proceed (and start sending/expecting messages) before post_writer's stream context was actually entered and ready, causing lost or hung messages during streamable-http POST writes. Both PRs fix it identically by adding a `task_status: TaskStatus[None]` parameter to `post_writer` and calling `task_status.started(None)` once the write-stream context is entered, so `tg.start()` callers block until post_writer is truly ready. (2 PRs)

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs touch the same lines in stdio_server that create the read/write memory object streams, both addressing the fact that the default buffer size of 0 (a rendezvous channel) can cause a stdout write to block a sender until a receiver is ready — e.g. queuing a handler's final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier progress notification. #2215 exposes read/write buffer sizes as new configurable constructor parameters but leaves the defaults at 0, so out-of-the-box behavior is unchanged unless a caller is also updated to pass a nonzero size (no such call-site change is included). #2654 instead hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1, directly changing default behavior, and adds a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the progress-notification blocking scenario.

members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2555: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: MCPError (specifically the UrlElicitationRequiredError subclass) cannot survive a pickle/unpickle round-trip because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), and self.args was set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data) — which doesn't match UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message=None) constructor signature, raising a TypeError on unpickle. members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py sends an error response when a request is cancelled, which violates the MCP/JSON-RPC spec requirement that receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request. Both PRs remove that error-response code from cancel(); #2493 additionally patches the caller-side duplicate-suppression log in server.py._handle_request, while #2514 also wires in emitting a spec-compliant `notifications/cancelled` message (importing CancelledNotificationParams) for both timeout and caller-initiated cancellation.
